page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance designed for workloads requiring extreme random-access memory density combined with high single-core CPU clock speeds. Built on dedicated hardware without hypervisor virtualization overhead, the server features an Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at up to 4.5 GHz across 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The system is provisioned with 1536 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, offering an extensive memory ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. Hardware support includes AVX-512 vector extensions, VNNI instructions, and AES cryptography acceleration.

The server delivers 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth but provides no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring persistent data to be attached over the network via Elastic Block Store or networked file systems. The configuration lacks discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput on large uncached memory reads (210.08 GB/sec) and writes (98.02 GB/sec), ranking in the top tier alongside a strong PassMark overall memory score of 2940.23. Compute performance reflects solid compilation throughput in Clang and strong PassMark CPU results, though multi-threaded decompression and standard database operations remain within median brackets.

Given the substantial memory capacity, cost efficiency is maximized when the massive RAM allocation is fully utilized rather than idling. While prompt processing for small and medium language models achieves average speeds, token generation rates remain weak due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. As a result, x2iezn.metal is primarily suited for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached distributed caches, electronic design automation (EDA), and memory-bound enterprise applications demanding non-virtualized bare-metal access.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for memory-heavy workloads requiring high single-core processor frequencies. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 24 physical cores, 48 dedicated vCPUs operating at up to 4.5 GHz, and 1536 GB of DDR4-3000 memory, establishing a 32 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration features 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and does not include graphics processing units. In benchmark assessments, x2iezn.metal achieves strong performance in large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth as well as software compilation tests, alongside balanced overall CPU compute results. Without hardware accelerators, text generation throughput for large models remains limited. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation, real-time analytics caching, and enterprise applications requiring bare-metal memory density.
